paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus sees the whole church, the good AND the not-so-good, and He says both out loud. To Pergamum He says they hold fast to His name, even where Satan's throne sits. Then He says He has a few things against them (Revelation 2:13-14). To Thyatira He says their latest deeds are greater than their first, and then He says they tolerate that woman Jezebel (Revelation 2:19-20). Praise and correction in the same letter. That's not Jesus being picky. That's Jesus paying attention.

Notice what He asks for, too. To both churches the call is plain: repent, and hold fast. Jesus tells Pergamum, "Therefore repent!" (Revelation 2:16), and He tells the rest of Thyatira to "hold fast to what you have until I come" (Revelation 2:25). Mixed-in teaching can sneak into a church, and it can sneak into you and me. I think the lesson is to stay close to what Jesus has already given us, and to turn back quick when something starts pulling us off. And Jesus says He is the One who "searches minds and hearts" (Revelation 2:23), so there's no faking it with Him. Good news, though: that also means nobody gets overlooked.

Then look at the promises. The hidden manna, a white stone with a new name known only to the one who receives it, authority shared from the Father, and the morning star (Revelation 2:17, 26-28). Every one of those goes to the one who overcomes. So keep going, baker. Hold on, keep doing His work, and keep your ear open. "He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches." (Revelation 2:29) This story isn't over, because there are more letters on the way.
